note.text:
Water moves continuously between the sea, the air, the land and living things: the water cycle.
• Evaporation: the sun heats seas, rivers and lakes; water vapour rises.
• Transpiration: plants lose water vapour from their leaves; with evaporation from soil it is evapotranspiration.
• Condensation: rising vapour cools and forms tiny droplets: clouds.
• Precipitation: droplets join and fall as rain (or hail).
• Infiltration (into the soil), runoff (into streams and rivers) and groundwater flow return water to the sea.
Animals take in water by drinking and in food, and return it by breathing out, sweating and excreting.

sections.heading: Water on the move
sections.text:
The same water has been used again and again for millions of years. It moves round and round between the sea, the air and the land: the water cycle.
The sun provides the energy: it heats seas, lakes and rivers, and water evaporates.

sections.heading: The main stages
sections.text:
• Evaporation: liquid water becomes vapour.
• Transpiration: plants release water vapour from their leaves.
• Condensation: vapour rises, cools and forms droplets: clouds and mist.
• Precipitation: droplets join and fall as rain.
• Infiltration and runoff: rain soaks into the soil or flows into streams, rivers and back to the sea.
Salt does not evaporate, so rain is fresh water.

sections.heading: Living things in the cycle
sections.text:
Plants take water from the soil and transpire it; animals drink and eat water and return it by breathing out, sweating and excreting.
Forests put a lot of water vapour into the air, so cutting them down can reduce local rainfall. Concrete and bare soil reduce infiltration and increase floods.

key_words.meaning: loss of water vapour from leaves

examples: Flooded streets after a storm: runoff

mistake.wrong: Clouds are made of water vapour
mistake.right: Clouds are made of tiny droplets of liquid water
mistake.why: Water vapour is invisible; clouds form when it condenses.

worked_example.problem: Describe the path of a drop of water from the Atlantic Ocean at Kribi to a farm near Ebolowa and back.
steps: The sun heats the sea: water evaporates.
The vapour rises, cools and condenses into clouds, which the wind carries inland.
Rain falls on the farm; some soaks into the soil and is taken up by plants, then transpired; some runs off into rivers that flow back to the ocean.
worked_example.answer: Evaporation → condensation → precipitation → infiltration/runoff (and transpiration) → back to the sea

pick.q: How do animals return water to the water cycle?
pick.r: By breathing out, sweating and excreting urine
e: They lose water in several ways.
pick.y: Water leaves animals as vapour and liquid.

pick.q: Why does cutting down large forests reduce rainfall in an area?
pick.r: Less transpiration puts less water vapour into the air
e: Trees release vapour; clouds form by condensation.
Forests do not cool the sea.
Most water passes through trees, not stays.
pick.y: Transpiration is a big source of vapour over land.

pick.q: What energy source drives the water cycle?
e: Wind moves clouds but the sun causes evaporation.
The moon causes tides, not evaporation.
Volcanoes are not the main driver.

pick.q: Rain water soaks into the soil.

pick.y: Water entering the soil is infiltration.
